title: Segmentized Prefix Store: segmentation & reclaimer notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an experimental design for a segmentized prefix store (SPS) and a lightweight reclaimer targeting fragmentation and tail-latency for long-running inference processes. The SPS idea: instead of a single monolithic KV arena, partition the prefix namespace into small fixed-size segments arranged by two orthogonal axes: sequence-length bands and temporal churn buckets. The goal is to reduce intra-segment fragmentation, improve locality for common sequence-length patterns, and make eviction decisions cost-aware (reassembly cost, serialization/deserialization).

High-level design goals:
1) low-latency lookup (single or two cache line probes for hot prefixes),
2) predictable reclaim cost (bounded background work),
3) memory compaction-friendly without stop-the-world pauses,
4) tenant-aware soft quotas and prefer-inplace-eviction for already-serialized spans.

Segment layout:
- Segment key: (tenant_id, seq_band, churn_bucket, lane_id) where
  - seq_band: discrete buckets like [<=32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2048, >2048] chosen from profile histograms.
  - churn_bucket: hot | warm | cold, assigned via an exponential decay of access timestamps sampled per prefix.
  - lane_id: small numeric shard to allow parallel allocation and reduce lock contention.
- Each segment contains a header with compact occupancy bitmap and a 16B sentinel table of slot metadata (4B hash, 4B tag, 8B payload/ref).
- Payloads for small prefixes (<=96 bytes) are packed inline into slots. Larger payloads are stored out-of-line in contiguous segment-run pages (growable).

Allocator and memory pools:
- Per-GPU pools: one pool per seq_band to match typical request memory shapes and kernel buffer planning. Pools use a bump-pointer freelist of fixed-size pages (e.g., 64KB) plus a lightweight per-lane freelist for micro-slices (<=512B).
- Coalescing policy: when adjacent out-of-line payloads free up within a segment-run, a background micro-defrag thread attempts to coalesce into a single run when the run occupancy falls below a threshold (e.g., 40%).
- Fallback pages: a small globally-shared emergency pool for cold large payloads to avoid allocation failures under spikes.

Eviction and reclaimer semantics:
- Primary eviction ordering: multi-queue combining churn_bucket (cold first) and a reuse-score computed from frequency and recency with exponential decay.
- Cost-aware eviction: estimated rehydrate-cost (CPU/GPU copy + deserial) is subtracted from reuse-score so we prefer evicting items that are cheap to reconstruct (e.g., small inlined tokens) under tight memory pressure.
- Batch reclaim strategy: reclaimers operate on a per-lane basis and perform three modes: fast-sample-eviction, compaction-pass, and slot-remap. Fast-sample-eviction is O(1) and uses reservoir sampling of candidate slots; compaction-pass migrates live payloads to new runs and flips metadata atomically. Slot-remap is used to collapse tombstones after multi-pass GC.

Fragmentation mitigation:
- Multi-pass approach: (1) opportunistic in-place free merging during low load; (2) periodic lightweight compaction on per-seq_band pools when fragmentation metrics exceed thresholds (free-run-count > X or avg-run-util < Y); (3) targeted rehoming for tenants that exceed fragmentation budgets.
- Observability signals: run_utilization_histogram, slot_tombstone_rate, avg_reclaim_bytes_per_second, compaction_latency_p99, per-tenant_fragmentation_score. These drive automated throttle/backoff for compaction.

Instrumentation & metrics to add:
- metric: sps.lookup_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99) per-seq_band
- metric: sps.eviction_candidates_per_reclaim
- metric: sps.coalesce_attempts_success_rate
- trace: reclaimer.compaction.{start,finish,aborted} with trace IDs tied to tenant and lane_id

Pseudocode (reclaimer fast path):
- periodically: for each lane in parallel:
    sample = reservoir_sample(lane.slots, k=16)
    candidates = filter(sample, is_evictable)
    rank = sort_by(cost_aware_score(candidates))
    evict_top_N(rank, N=target)

cost_aware_score(item) = reuse_score(item) - alpha * rehydrate_cost(item)
rehydrate_cost(item) approx= payload_bytes / cpu_bandwidth + gpu_copy_time_estimate

Open questions / risks:
- Are seq_band boundaries optimal for multimodal workloads? Need automated band recomputation and safe migration strategy.
- Coalescing may introduce cross-lane coordination; need to ensure we don't create lock storms.
- Out-of-line run coalescing has potential to increase GPU memcpy overhead during compaction; set conservative thresholds for live traffic.
- Long-lived tenants can fragment many segments; need tenant throttles and a tenant-level compaction budget.

Experiments & rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (lab): implement SPS in-memory structure, run offline simulation with replay traces (public trace + internal production sample). Compare avg lookup latency and p50/p99 GC pause vs current slab allocator.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable SPS for 2 non-critical tenants on a dedicated Dedicated pool. Observe metrics for 72 hours. Feature flag: sps.enabled=true per-tenant.
- Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 20% of traffic with automatic fallback to legacy allocator on SLO breach. Keep compaction disabled by default, enable only if fragmentation_score > threshold.

Migration considerations:
- On enable: only new prefixes are placed into SPS; existing prefixes left in legacy allocator until TTL or explicit migration pass.
- Safe rollback: metadata versioning per-segment. If rollback, map new reads to legacy store via fast-path translation layer.

Work items (short):
- [ ] implement segment header + occupancy bitmap (Luca)
- [ ] add runtime metrics and tracing hooks (Priya)
- [ ] reservoir sampling eviction prototype (Jordan)
- [ ] offline simulator integration and trace harness (Samira)
- [ ] experiment dashboard and alerting thresholds (SRE)

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally rough. Focus feedback on: memory pool sizing heuristics, seq_band boundaries, and eviction scoring weights (alpha).
- Related: see github PR 1893 for an initial allocator shim and ENG-762 for scheduling-level cooperation with request batching.

Unresolved knobs (for follow-up doc):
- exact page sizes per seq_band, adaptive lane count per-GPU, compaction pacing algorithm (linear vs token-rate proportional), tenant fragmentation budgets and billing implications.

End of note.
